entries.1:1: Peter introduces himself as a messenger sent by Jesus and addresses followers of Jesus scattered across several regions. It reminds readers that they belong to Christ no matter where they live.
entries.1:2: God chose these believers, set them apart by his Spirit, and cleansed them through Jesus' sacrifice. Peter wishes them real grace and peace, which is what God offers each of us.
entries.1:3: God's mercy gave believers a fresh start and a hope that won't die, secured by Jesus rising from the dead. This gives the reader solid reason to praise God.
entries.1:4: God is keeping an inheritance for believers that is pure, lasting, and untouched by decay. It means the future God promises you is safe and cannot be lost.
entries.1:5: God's power guards believers through their trust in him until the full salvation he has prepared is revealed. You are being kept safe by God himself, not by your own strength.
entries.1:6: Despite present troubles and testing, believers have deep reason to rejoice because their hope is secure. Hard times are real but temporary compared to what God has promised.
entries.1:7: Trials refine faith the way fire refines gold, showing it to be far more valuable. Your struggles are not wasted; they prove your faith genuine and bring honor to Jesus.
entries.1:8: Believers love and trust Jesus even without seeing him, and that produces joy too deep for words. Faith in someone unseen can still fill your life with real gladness.
entries.1:9: The goal of trusting Jesus is the salvation of your whole self. Your faith is heading somewhere real: rescue and wholeness from God.
entries.1:10: The prophets of old studied carefully the salvation and grace that would later come to believers. It shows God's plan was long in the making and worth searching for.
entries.1:11: The Spirit within the prophets pointed ahead to Christ's sufferings and the glory that would follow. God's plan included the hard parts, not just the good ones.
entries.1:12: The prophets learned their message was for future believers, not themselves, and even angels long to understand it. You are receiving something generations longed to see.
entries.1:13: Peter tells believers to think clearly, stay alert, and set their full hope on the grace coming when Jesus returns. It calls the reader to stay focused and hopeful.
entries.1:14: As God's children, believers should not slip back into the selfish desires they had before they knew better. Knowing God should change how you live.
entries.1:15: Believers are to be holy in every part of life, just as the God they serve is holy. It means letting God's character shape your everyday choices.
entries.1:16: Scripture itself commands God's people to be holy because God is holy. The standard for your life comes from who God is, not from what others do.
entries.1:17: Since God judges fairly and shows no favoritism, believers should live with reverent respect during their time on earth. It means taking your conduct seriously before a fair God.
entries.1:18: Believers were freed from an empty way of life inherited from their ancestors, and not by money or anything perishable. Your freedom cost something far greater than wealth.
entries.1:19: The price paid was the blood of Christ, pictured as a perfect, spotless lamb. God freed you at great personal cost to himself.
entries.1:20: Christ was chosen for this purpose before the world began and appeared in these times for your sake. It shows you were on God's mind from the very start.
entries.1:21: Through Christ, believers trust in the God who raised him from the dead and glorified him. Your faith and hope can rest firmly in God himself.
entries.1:22: Having purified yourselves by obeying the truth, believers are to love each other sincerely and deeply. Real love for others should be warm and honest, not fake.
entries.1:23: Believers have been born again through God's living and lasting word, not through anything human and temporary. Your new life comes from something that never wears out.
entries.1:24: Scripture compares human life to grass and flowers that dry up and fade. It reminds the reader that everything merely human is brief and fragile.
entries.1:25: Unlike grass and flowers, the word of the Lord lasts forever, and this is the good news preached to believers. The message you have heard is permanent and trustworthy.
entries.2:1: Stop doing wrong things like lying, cheating, jealousy, and gossip. These things damage your relationships and don't belong in your life as a follower of Jesus.
entries.2:2: Just like a baby eagerly wants milk, you should deeply want to learn and grow from God's word. This hunger helps you grow stronger in your faith and move toward what God has for you.
entries.2:3: You have already experienced how kind and good the Lord is. That experience should make you want to keep growing closer to him.
entries.2:4: Jesus is like a living stone that people rejected, but God sees him as extremely valuable. You come to him as the foundation of your faith.
entries.2:5: You are like living stones being built together into a spiritual house where God dwells. As part of this, you serve as priests who offer spiritual sacrifices that please God through Jesus.
entries.2:6: God placed Jesus as the most important stone in the building, and he is precious beyond measure. Anyone who trusts in him will never be disappointed or let down.
entries.2:7: For those who believe, Jesus is incredibly valuable. But for those who don't believe, he is the stone the builders rejected that became the most important part of the building.
entries.2:8: For those who don't believe, Jesus is like a stone that makes them stumble and fall. They trip over him because they refuse to obey God's word, and this was always part of God's plan.
entries.2:9: You are a chosen people, a holy nation, and a royal priesthood belonging completely to God. Your purpose is to tell others about the wonderful things God did by bringing you from darkness into his marvelous light.
entries.2:10: At one time you weren't considered God's people, but now you are. You hadn't received mercy before, but now God has shown you great mercy.
entries.2:11: As people who are just passing through this world like foreigners, stay away from sinful desires. These desires fight against your soul and pull you away from God.
entries.2:12: Live good and honest lives among those who don't believe. Even if they accuse you of doing wrong now, your good actions will make them praise God when he comes to judge.
entries.2:13: Obey human authorities and laws out of respect for the Lord. This includes the king or whoever is in the highest position of power.
entries.2:14: Obey the officials the king appoints to punish those who do wrong and to praise those who do right. Respecting these leaders honors God.
entries.2:15: God wants your good behavior to silence the ignorant and foolish people who criticize you. Your actions speak louder than their accusations.
entries.2:16: You are free in Christ, but don't use that freedom as an excuse to do wrong. Instead, live as people who are fully devoted to serving God.
entries.2:17: Show respect to everyone, love your fellow believers deeply, honor God with reverence, and respect the king. Each of these relationships requires a different kind of honor.
entries.2:18: If you work for someone, respect and obey your employer—not just when they are kind and fair, but even when they are harsh and difficult.
entries.2:19: It pleases God when you endure unfair suffering because you are trying to do what is right before him. This kind of patient endurance shows God's grace at work in you.
entries.2:20: There's no credit in quietly accepting punishment when you deserve it for doing wrong. But if you suffer for doing right and endure it patiently, this pleases God.
entries.2:21: God called you to this kind of patient endurance because Christ himself suffered for you. He left you an example to follow closely in his steps.
entries.2:22: Jesus never sinned and never lied or deceived anyone. He was completely pure and honest in everything he did and said.
entries.2:23: When people insulted Jesus, he didn't insult them back. When he suffered, he didn't threaten revenge but trusted himself to God, who judges fairly.
entries.2:24: Jesus carried our sins in his own body on the cross so that we could stop sinning and start living rightly. Through his wounds and suffering, we are healed and made whole.
entries.2:25: You used to wander away like lost sheep, each going your own way. But now you have returned to Jesus, who watches over and cares for your souls.
entries.3:1: Wives are told to follow their husbands' leadership so that a husband who ignores God's word might be won over by how his wife lives. Your everyday conduct can speak louder than any argument.
entries.3:2: The husband is won over by seeing his wife live a pure, respectful life shaped by her reverence for God. What you do matters more than what you say.
entries.3:3: Peter isn't banning nice hair or jewelry or clothes; he's saying outward decoration shouldn't be the main thing you're known for. Don't let your appearance be your whole identity.
entries.3:4: The real beauty God values is inward: a calm, gentle spirit that doesn't wear out. That kind of character is precious to God and worth building.
entries.3:5: Holy women of the past made God their hope and showed this same inward beauty by respecting their husbands. You can follow their example of trusting God.
entries.3:6: Sarah respected Abraham and called him her lord, and you are her spiritual daughters if you do good and don't give in to fear. Do what's right without being paralyzed by threats.
entries.3:7: Husbands must live thoughtfully with their wives, honoring them as weaker in body yet equally heirs of God's gift of life. Treating a wife badly damages your own prayer life.
entries.3:8: All believers should be united in mind, sympathetic, loving each other as family, compassionate, and humble. These attitudes hold a community together.
entries.3:9: Don't repay insults or harm with the same; instead respond with blessing, because God has called you to inherit blessing. Your response can break the cycle of retaliation.
entries.3:10: If you want to enjoy life and see good days, keep your tongue from evil and your lips from lying. Watch your words if you want a good life.
entries.3:11: Turn away from evil and do good; actively hunt for peace and pursue it. Peace doesn't just happen—you have to go after it.
entries.3:12: The Lord watches over righteous people and listens to their prayers, but he sets himself against those who do evil. God sees how you live and hears you when you pray.
entries.3:13: If you are eager to do good, who is really going to harm you? Goodness usually protects you, so don't live in fear of others.
entries.3:14: Even if you suffer for doing right, you are blessed; don't be afraid of what frightens others or let it shake you. Suffering for good doesn't mean God has abandoned you.
entries.3:15: Set Christ apart as Lord in your heart and always be ready to explain the hope you have—respectfully and humbly. Know why you believe so you can answer kindly when asked.
entries.3:16: Keep a clear conscience so that those who insult your good Christian life will end up ashamed of their slander. Live so your accusers have nothing real to hold against you.
entries.3:17: If God allows you to suffer, it's better to suffer for doing good than for doing wrong. Your suffering has more meaning when your conduct is right.
entries.3:18: Christ suffered once for sins, the righteous dying for the unrighteous, to bring us to God; he was put to death physically but made alive by the Spirit. His sacrifice is how you can be reconciled to God.
entries.3:19: In the Spirit, Christ went and preached to imprisoned spirits. This shows Christ's victory reaches even those held in the realm of the dead.
entries.3:20: These were the spirits who disobeyed long ago during Noah's time, when God patiently waited while the ark was built and only eight people were saved through water. God is patient, but rescue comes through trusting him.
entries.3:21: Baptism pictures this salvation: it saves you not by physically washing dirt away but by a clean conscience before God, through Jesus' resurrection. What matters is your heart's response to God, not just the water.
entries.3:22: Christ has gone into heaven and sits at God's right hand, with angels and all authorities and powers under his rule. Jesus is in charge, so you can trust his power over everything.
entries.4:1: Jesus suffered and died as a human being, and Peter tells us to think the same way. When we are willing to give up our old selfish life, sin loses its grip on us.
entries.4:2: The rest of your life should not be spent chasing what people want, but doing what God wants. Your time belongs to God now, not to your own cravings.
entries.4:3: You have already spent enough time living the way people who don't know God live, chasing pleasure, drinking, wild parties, and false worship. That old life is over and done with.
entries.4:4: People are surprised that you no longer join them in their reckless, wasteful living, and they insult you for it. Expect that reaction rather than being shocked by it.
entries.4:5: Those who mock you will have to answer to God, who is ready to judge everyone, both the living and the dead. No one escapes giving an account to him.
entries.4:6: This is why the good news was preached even to those who have died, so that although they were judged as ordinary humans, they could live with God in the spirit. Death does not cut people off from God's offer of life.
entries.4:7: The end of all things is near, so stay clear-headed and watchful, and keep praying. Live each day as though time is short.
entries.4:8: Above everything else, love each other deeply, because love covers over a great many sins. Real love forgives and does not keep a record of wrongs.
entries.4:9: Welcome others into your home gladly, without grumbling about it. Hospitality should be given freely and cheerfully.
entries.4:10: Each of you has been given gifts by God, so use them to serve one another as good managers of his generous grace. Your gifts are not for you alone.
entries.4:11: If you speak, speak as one speaking God's words; if you serve, serve with the strength God supplies, so that in everything God gets the glory through Jesus Christ. Everything you do should point people to God, not to yourself.
entries.4:12: Don't be surprised when your faith is tested by hard times, as though something strange were happening to you. Testing is a normal part of following Christ.
entries.4:13: Instead, be glad that you share in Christ's sufferings, so that when his glory is revealed you will be filled with joy. Present pain leads to future joy.
entries.4:14: If people insult you because you belong to Christ, you are blessed, because God's Spirit of glory rests on you. Insults for Christ's sake are not a sign of failure but of God's presence.
entries.4:15: None of you should suffer as a murderer, thief, wrongdoer, or someone who meddles in other people's affairs. Suffering that comes from your own wrongdoing is a different matter.
entries.4:16: But if you suffer because you are a Christian, don't be ashamed; instead, praise God for the name you bear. Being identified with Christ is something to be honored, even when it costs you.
entries.4:17: The time has come for judgment to begin with God's own people. If it starts with us, think how much more serious it will be for those who have not obeyed God. God's judgment is real, and it begins close to home.
entries.4:18: If even a good person is saved only with difficulty, what will happen to the ungodly and the sinner? Salvation is serious business, not something to take for granted.
entries.4:19: So those who suffer according to God's will should keep doing good and entrust themselves to their faithful Creator. Keep doing right and trust your life to the God who made you and is faithful.
entries.5:1: Peter introduces himself as a fellow church leader who saw Christ's suffering and shares in the glory to come, so his request to the leaders carries real weight. He speaks as an equal, not a distant authority.
entries.5:2: Leaders are to care for the people God has placed in their charge, serving willingly and honestly rather than out of obligation or greed. The reader should expect leaders to serve gladly, and leaders should examine their own motives.
entries.5:3: Leaders must not boss people around but should set a good example others can follow. This means influence comes through how you live, not through control.
entries.5:4: When Christ, the true head shepherd, returns, faithful leaders will receive lasting honor from him. The reward for humble service comes from God, not from people.
entries.5:5: Younger people should accept the guidance of older ones, and everyone should be humble and ready to serve rather than proud. God opposes pride but gives grace to the humble, so humility is the safer path.
entries.5:6: Humble yourself under God's authority now, trusting that he will raise you up at the right time. You can let go of self-promotion because God handles your honor.
entries.5:7: Give your worries to God because he genuinely cares about you. You do not have to carry your anxieties alone.
entries.5:8: Stay alert and clear-headed, because the devil is actively looking for someone to harm, like a lion hunting prey. Spiritual danger is real, so watchfulness matters.
entries.5:9: Resist the devil by standing firm in your faith, remembering that believers everywhere face the same kinds of struggles. You are not alone in your suffering.
entries.5:10: After a short time of suffering, the God of grace will himself restore, strengthen, and establish you in his eternal glory through Christ. Your pain is temporary, and God promises to make you whole.
entries.5:11: God holds all power forever, and this is certain. The reader can rest in the fact that God's strength never runs out.
entries.5:12: Peter sent this brief letter through Silvanus to encourage the readers and confirm that what they received is the true grace of God. They should stand firm in it.
entries.5:13: The church in Babylon, along with Mark, sends greetings to the readers. This shows the readers they are part of a wider family of believers who care about them.
entries.5:14: Greet each other with genuine love, and may peace be with all who belong to Christ. The letter ends by calling for warm, sincere relationships within the church.
